title: GS Retail launches AI startup PoCs to drive on-site retail transformation in Korea - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
content: GS Retail(26,450 won ▲ 50 0.19%) said on the 20th that it held the 4th cohort meetup for the open innovation program "The GS Challenge Future Retail" at GS Tower in Gangnam District, Seoul, on the 16th, and began proof-of-concept (PoC) projects with five AI startups that were finally selected. GS Retail aims to fully push an on-site focused AX (AI transformation) project that integrates the technology of AI startups into retail operations to solve practical tasks. This year's program proceeded by having business units first present tasks that need to be solved on the ground and then finding startups with the technology and execution capability to carry them out. Whereas cohorts 1 to 3 collaborated with startups centered on technology, starting with the 4th cohort the focus shifted to strengthening consolidation between on-the-job tasks and external technologies. In designing the program, GS Retail surveyed 17 business units companywide for the necessary technologies and problems to solve. Based on this, it set three core areas—data/AI intelligence, autonomous operations optimization, and digital customer engagement innovation—and selected five startups with high potential for business application. GS Retail's business units and the participating startups will run proof-of-concept projects using AI technology for about four months from this meetup through mid-November. Key tasks include a project that uses vision AI to analyze the behavior and purchasing patterns of customers visiting fresh-food specialty stores. It will also pursue generative engine optimization (GEO) to respond to the search environment shifting around Generative AI and AI-based customer relationship management (CRM) automation. A proof-of-concept project will also be carried out to identify products likely to see rising consumer interest by analyzing social media data and to nurture new brands based on influencer and fandom data. To increase the intensity of collaboration with startups, GS Retail narrowed this year's selected companies to five. Before the full selection, it strengthened the review process by holding prior consultations between business units and startups to examine task–technology fit and real-world applicability. It also plans to expand the scale of support allocated to some proof-of-concept projects by linking with government support programs. Meanwhile, a total of seven corporations were selected for the 3rd cohort, and they jointly developed with GS Retail solutions such as short-form creation automation, an AI-based 3D content generation platform, and a Gen AI-based commercial content creation solution. Lee Seong-hwa, head of new growth at GS Retail, said, "The core of AX innovation with startups is consolidation of excellent technology with tangible customer value and business performance," adding, "Through this 4th cohort, we will further advance Future Retail as an open innovation platform that links solving on-the-job tasks with business application." title: This 10-Year-Old Japanese Sedan's Interior Is Better Than Most New German Rivals - CarBuzz
content: The fourth-generation Lexus GS proves that great cabin design doesn't expire with age. Marking the end of the GS nameplate, this surprisingly spirited midsize luxury sedan pairs impeccable build quality with timeless styling, premium materials, and ergonomics that still outshine many newer German competitors. Buyers have noticed. The final GS has held its value remarkably well, so don't expect bargain-bin pricing just because it's a decade old. Its combination of reliability, refinement, and a genuinely upscale interior keeps demand high, and used prices reflect that. The Lexus GS always occupied a sweet spot in the fiercely contested midsize luxury sedan segment. It combines the balanced handling of a rear-wheel-drive sports sedan with the supple ride, refinement, and rock-solid reliability that have long defined the Lexus brand. That formula earned it a loyal following, but it couldn't escape the market's relentless shift toward SUVs. Lexus finally pulled the plug on the GS after the 2020 model year, leaving the similarly sized but front-wheel-drive ES as its midsize luxury sedan. It's an understandable decision, even if the ES lacks the GS' driver-focused character. By 2019, the GS accounted for just four percent of Lexus' US sales, with only 3,378 examples finding homes that year. The fourth-generation version was introduced for the 2013 model year after making an unlikely debut during 2011 Monterey Car Week. It's the version to buy today because it represents the peak evolution of the GS formula, blending handsome styling, sharp dynamics, and quality that still feels competitive nearly a decade later. Lexus gave the car a mid-cycle refresh for 2016, sharpening the styling, updating the technology, and introducing the fire-breathing GS F V8 flagship. The cabin changed very little, though, so pre-facelift models shouldn't be dismissed outright. Even so, if your budget allows, the refreshed car is the better pick thanks to its improved technology, particularly when it comes to safety, and broader range of powertrain options. Performance enthusiasts should head straight for the GS F. Its naturally aspirated 5.0-liter V8 produces 467 horsepower and 389 pound-feet of torque, and its legendary durability already makes it feel like a future classic. Buyers who don't need that level of performance will still find plenty to like elsewhere in the lineup. Following the 2016 refresh, the range opened with the GS 200t, which used a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-four producing 241 hp and 258 lb-ft. Above it sat the GS 350 with a then-new 3.5-liter V6 delivering 311 hp and 280 lb-ft, while the GS 450h paired a 3.5-liter V6 with an electric motor for a combined 338 hp and 254 lb-ft of torque. But powertrains are easy to compare – what makes the GS genuinely hard to replace is what happens once you're inside. The same philosophy that shaped the GS's rear-wheel-drive chassis – prioritize what matters, ignore what doesn't – defined its interior, too. The GS doesn't rely on flashy design tricks (ambient lighting, anyone?) or acres of digital screens to impress, and that's exactly why it has aged so gracefully. Instead of chasing the latest trends, Lexus focused on the fundamentals. The dashboard is clean and uncluttered, with physical buttons and knobs for the functions you use most, along with analog gauges, premium leather, genuine wood or aluminum trim, and soft-touch materials on nearly every surface your hands naturally reach. While there's still a 12.3-inch infotainment screen, it doesn't dominate the dash, and you won't find glossy piano-black panels waiting to collect fingerprints. One of the cabin's biggest highlights, and today, a genuine flex, is the beautifully refined analog clock sitting proudly at the center of the dash. It evokes the classic luxury sedans of the past, yet it's far more sophisticated than its traditional appearance suggests. Lexus machined the clock from a single ingot of aluminum, making it look like a high-end watch. Meanwhile, LED backlighting ensures it's easy to read at night, while GPS synchronization automatically adjusts the time when traveling across time zones. It's just the type of feature that reflects the GS' attention to detail. The rest of the cabin follows the same approach, packing in luxury features without making them feel overwhelming. Even standard models came well-equipped with power-adjustable heated front seats, dual-zone climate control, and keyless entry and start, while higher trims added ventilated seats, heated rear seats, premium semi-aniline leather upholstery, a power rear sunshade, and higher-quality dash accents. Audiophiles should also seek out models equipped with the available 17-speaker Mark Levinson surround-sound system, which remains one of the best factory audio systems of its era. The pre-facelifted GS shares the same basic cabin design, so buyers on a tighter budget won't be missing out too much. However, it lacks a few of the later car's finer touches, including the GPS-synchronized analog clock, the 4.2-inch multifunction display in the gauge cluster, and the updated steering wheel design. It also missed out on the Lexus Safety System+ suite of electronic driver-assist features that debuted with the 2016 update. The suite bundles Adaptive Cruise Control, Pre-Collision System with Pedestrian Detection, Lane Keep Assist, Automatic High Beams, Sway Warning, Traffic Sign Recognition, and more. As with most Lexus vehicles, the fourth-generation GS delivers impressive reliability. RepairPal gives it an above-average four-out-of-five-star reliability rating, ranking it among the best cars in its class, while listing annual repair costs as well below the segment average. CarComplaints also records relatively few owner-reported issues, though the car's initial 2013 model year seems to have significantly more reported issues than any other year, most of them electronic gremlins. Despite its strong reliability ratings, not every GS will be trouble-free. Like any aging luxury car, maintenance history matters far more than the badge on the hood. Make sure routine servicing has been carried out, inspect the suspension for wear (especially on higher-mileage cars), and verify that all recalls have been completed, including those affecting earlier model years related to the Takata airbag scandal. Ironically, the interior is not without one key quality issue, at least on pre-facelift GS models. The dashboard material can be susceptible to heat and prolonged sun exposure, causing the upper dash to become sticky or even crack over time. It's worth checking the dashboard and door panels for tackiness or discoloration before buying, although many affected cars have already been repaired. Lexus largely addressed the issue with the facelifted model. A quick look through the CarBuzz Marketplace and other popular classifieds shows that fourth-generation GS prices start below $10,000, but those cars are typically pre-facelift models with close to 200,000 miles on the odometer. Set a more realistic mileage cap of around 70,000 miles, and you'll find plenty of well-kept examples priced from roughly $20,000. If your sights are set on the updated 2016-2020 model, however, expect to spend at least $25,000 for a clean example with reasonable mileage. Those asking prices highlight just how well the GS has held its value. The 2016 lineup started at $45,615 for the GS 200t, powered by the turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder, while the much more common GS 350 carried a starting MSRP of $50,000. Considering that most low-mileage, facelifted GS 350s still command around half of their original sticker price nearly a decade later, depreciation has been surprisingly gentle. That's an impressive showing in a segment where many luxury sedans lose value rapidly during their first few years. The GS F sits in an entirely different league. Thanks to its naturally aspirated 2UR-GSE 5.0-liter V8 and growing reputation as a future classic, prices remain remarkably strong. Expect to pay at least $50,000, with clean, well-maintained examples more commonly advertised around $60,000. That's not far removed from the 2016 model's $84,440 starting MSRP. Now compare that with similarly aged BMW M5 and Mercedes-AMG E63 models, both of which have depreciated far more heavily despite offering comparable performance. The fourth-generation Lexus GS is proof that great luxury cars don't have to chase trends to stay relevant. Its well-built, thoughtfully designed cabin still feels special nearly a decade later, while strong reliability, a sporty rear-wheel-drive chassis, and impressive value retention only strengthen its appeal. If you're shopping for a used midsize luxury sedan and are the type who likes to hold on to a car, few alternatives blend craftsmanship, comfort, and driving enjoyment quite as convincingly. title: Karol G's Blueprint for Modern Pop Stardom - Young Hollywood
content: The Colombian superstar's global takeover isn't just about music. It's a masterclass in color, confidence, and community. Karol G's rise to the top proves the old rules of pop stardom are over. We're breaking down how her vibrant visual identity and fan-first ethos created a global movement. The old playbook for becoming a global pop icon has been officially shredded. For decades, the path was narrow: sing in English, sand down your edges, and fit a pre-approved mold. But a new generation of artists is proving that true superstardom is built on authenticity, not assimilation. And right now, no one is making a more vibrant and compelling case for that than Karol G. The Colombian powerhouse isn't just topping charts; she's building an entire world. Her success is a technicolor phenomenon that moves through sight and sound in equal measure, proving that a powerful message, a distinct look, and a real community can resonate in any language. It’s a blueprint for stardom that feels radically new, yet fundamentally human. Let’s talk about the hair. When Karol G transitioned into her brilliant blue era, and later her radiant pink phase for the Mañana Será Bonito chapter, it was more than a style refresh. It became a powerful piece of visual branding, an immediate signifier of who she is and what her music feels like. It was a beacon that fans, and the world, could instantly recognize. This use of color is a core part of her genius. It’s an unspoken language that telegraphs emotion, confidence, and transformation. At her stadium shows, seas of pink wigs and merchandise aren’t just fans showing support; they’re participants in a shared visual experience. It transforms a concert into a collective statement, creating an instantly iconic image that spreads organically across every social feed on the planet. This is how you build a universe, not just a fanbase. For years, the industry pushed the idea that massive international success required 'crossing over' into English-language music. Karol G politely ignored that memo. By continuing to create primarily in Spanish, she has centered her culture and experience, inviting the world to meet her where she is. Spoiler alert: the world showed up. In a hyper-connected streaming era, authenticity is the ultimate currency, and her commitment to her language is a huge part of that. It allows the emotion and swagger in her delivery to land with its full, undiluted power. Listeners who don’t speak Spanish don’t feel excluded; they feel the confidence, the vulnerability, and the joy. It bypasses literal translation and connects on the level of pure feeling, proving that a banger is a banger in any tongue. Her music itself defies easy categorization, pulling from reggaeton, pop, and Latin trap to create a sound that is uniquely her own. This genre-fluid approach ensures her art is never static, always reflecting a genuine place of inspiration rather than chasing a trend. It’s another way she asserts her vision, free from the constraints of outdated industry boxes. Beyond the visuals and the sonics, the core of Karol G’s empire is the community she has cultivated. It’s built on the powerful concept of the 'Bichota'—a term she has helped popularize to mean a confident, empowered, and unapologetic woman. It’s not just a cool word; it’s an ethos. She doesn’t just perform for her fans; she empowers them. This idea of collective confidence is woven through her entire creative output. She shares her own journey of growth and self-love, creating a space where vulnerability is a strength. Her connection feels less like an artist-to-fan dynamic and more like a massive, global friend group where everyone is cheering each other on. It’s this profound sense of belonging that turns casual listeners into die-hard devotees. That fan connection is the engine behind her record-breaking tours and chart dominance. People aren’t just buying a ticket to hear songs they like; they’re showing up for a reaffirming, communal experience. It’s a testament to the fact that in 2024, the most powerful marketing tool is a genuine, two-way relationship built on respect and shared values. Karol G is more than a pop star. She's a cultural force demonstrating a new path forward. title: Vernon Ice Cream Shop Invites Community Back For Free Cone Day On July 19 - Patch
content: VERNON, CT — Frankie G’s Ice Cream is inviting the community to return for its National Ice Cream Day celebration on Sunday, July 19, with free cones available for part of the day. The shop said it welcomed more than 600 friends, families and neighbors to last year’s event and is planning another afternoon gathering this summer. From 12 p.m. to 3 p.m., Frankie G’s at 448 Hartford Turnpike will give away free regular-size ice cream cones. The offer includes a choice of flavor and sprinkles, with one cone available per person. According to the event announcement, each person must be present to receive the free cone. The promotion will be available at the walk-up window only. Frankie G’s also said the shop will be open from 12 p.m. to 9 p.m., with its full menu available throughout the day for customers who want additional items beyond the giveaway. The event is centered on National Ice Cream Day and is framed by the business as a community celebration tied to summer. In its announcement, Frankie G’s described the day as “the perfect excuse to get together, enjoy a sweet treat, and celebrate summer.” The shop also said, “Whether you’re a returning guest or visiting for the first time, everyone is welcome to stop by, enjoy a free cone, and be part of another fun-filled community celebration at Frankie G’s Ice Cream.” The announcement invites both repeat customers and first-time visitors to attend. People planning to go should keep the event rules in mind before arriving. The free cone offer is limited to a regular-size cone, applies only from noon to 3 p.m., and is restricted to one per person. The person receiving the cone must be there in person, and the promotion will not be offered anywhere except the walk-up window. For the rest of the day, Frankie G’s will continue regular operations until 9 p.m. with its standard menu available. The free giveaway is scheduled to end at 3 p.m., while the larger National Ice Cream Day celebration will continue as part of the shop’s regular business hours. title: Future “Flying G’s” learn from varsity players at Gladwin’s Youth Football Camp - WNEM
content: GLADWIN, Mich. (WNEM) - Gladwin Varsity Football got to give back to the community as the team held their annual Tim Foor Youth Football Camp. The three-day event featured boys and girls from 1st through 6th grade learning about football with focus on fundamentals, effort and character. “When we first started eight years ago Marc and I, we had maybe 10 kids at the camp,” said Gladwin Head Football Coach Kody Emeott. “It definitely wasn’t as big as it is now and every year it’s just grown a little bit bigger.” Emeott recently became the new Head Coach of the Varsity Football Team and today his players were out running the individual drills for the campers. “Our kids pretty much run the whole thing,” said Emeott. “I just kind of time manage everything. So it gets not just our Varsity, but our whole high school program, it gets them around kids which a lot of times they’re not and to kind of be great role models for them in that sense.” Some of the varsity players have experienced being a camper here as young kids. Now they’re excited to lead the way for the new campers with dreams of playing on Friday Nights. “I remember coming here as a kid and learning from the guys before me, so it feels really good to get out here and give back to the program that built me,” said Gladwin Senior Max Barz. “It’s really crucial because they’re at the age right now where they’re trying to figure out what sports to play and if we can get them to play football, then that’s really important to us.”

title: Why Did Banking Stocks GS, JPM, BAC Surge To 52-Week Highs Today? - Stocktwits
content: Shares of Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (GS), JPMorgan Chase & Co. (JPM), and Bank of America Corp. (BAC) surged to annual highs after the banks posted stellar second-quarter earnings results that beat market expectations. GS stock led the climb among banking stocks, surging more than 9% after its record Q2 results triggered a buy-in. JPM stock rose 2.5% after its results surged past Wall Street expectations, while BAC stock also soared nearly 2% to a record high. GS stock climbed to a record high of $1,143.84 on Tuesday after the company reported record Q2 results that tore past analysts’ expectations. Goldman Sachs posted quarterly revenue of $20.98 billion, significantly higher than Wall Street's $16.4 billion estimate, according to Koyfin data. The investment bank also reported earnings of $15.91 per share, ahead of the $14.40 consensus estimate, while net income reached a record $6.32 billion for the quarter. The strong results were fueled by robust performance in investment banking, equities trading, and asset management, as companies continued to tap capital markets and pursue AI-related financing and strategic deals. "There's a lot of capital out there," CEO David Solomon said in an interview with CNBC on Tuesday. "I'm not concerned about the ability for the capital to be available for things that make sense." GS stock has surged nearly 25% so far this year. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment was ‘extremely bullish’ at the time of writing. JPM stock climbed to a 52-week high of $344.73 on Tuesday, driven by strong Q2 results that boosted investor interest in the company. The bank posted revenue of $57.35 billion versus a consensus estimate of $51.3 billion, while earnings per share (EPS) came in at $7.70 per share versus an expectation of $ 5.80 per share, based on Fiscal.ai data. JPMorgan delivered its strongest trading quarter on record, with trading revenue jumping 35% year over year to $12.1 billion. CEO Jamie Dimon said every business segment achieved record results, noting that market conditions remain favorable for sustained activity. Investment banking fees climbed 30% from a year earlier to $3.3 billion, marking their highest level since 2021, while net interest income rose 10% year over year to $25.6 billion. Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs raised the price target on the bank to $418 from $411 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating on the shares after its Q2 earnings beat, as per TheFly. JPM stock has gained more than 5% so far this year as retail sentiment improved from ‘bullish’ to ‘extremely bullish’ over 24 hours. BAC stock also climbed to a record high of $61.21 on Tuesday, driven by Q2 results that demonstrated a strong investment banking pipeline amid growing AI demand. The bank reported revenue of $31.6 billion, ahead of analyst estimates of $30.7 billion. Meanwhile, earnings per share (EPS) came in at $1.21, beating expectations of $1.13 EPS. Investment banking revenue climbed 50% year-over-year, with sales and trading revenue rising 30%. A surge of more than 70% in equities trading was the standout performer, contributing to one of the bank's best quarters in recent years. "We still have very strong pipelines in investment banking. The IPOs and deals are still getting done, and very strong interest in doing transactions,” CEO Brian Moynihan told CNBC in an interview. "The AI buildout still has a lot of debt funding and other funding required, so it's a very good environment." Meanwhile, Jefferies raised the price target on Bank of America to $75 from $70 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating on the shares after a "strong quarter," as per TheFly. The steep decline followed reports that restructuring adviser AlixPartners was reviewing options for the company, including possibilities that investors interpreted as potential bankruptcy or a private-market transaction. Lucid moved quickly to deny the claims, saying the bankruptcy-related speculation was “completely false.” The company said AlixPartners was assisting with operational improvements, including cost management, manufacturing efficiency and supply-chain efforts rather than preparing for insolvency proceedings. The company’s stock has declined 33% over the past month as concerns about spending, financing needs, and customer concentration have overshadowed optimism about its large cloud business. Oracle has a huge backlog of cloud orders, but the company is taking on more debt to build the data centers needed to complete those contracts. A major factor weighing on Oracle has been a downgrade from S&P Global, which lowered the company’s credit rating to BBB-, only one level above non-investment-grade status. The agency highlighted concerns about Oracle’s reliance on large customers, including OpenAI, which represents a large portion of its remaining performance obligations. U.S. stock futures edged higher in the overnight session late Tuesday as softer-than-expected inflation data boosted technology stocks and eased rate hike concerns, overshadowing escalating tensions between the U.S. and Iran. Meanwhile, strong quarterly results from top banks on Tuesday reinforced market confidence in a solid earnings season. Dow futures were up 0.05%, S&P 500 futures climbed 0.18%, and Nasdaq-100 futures climbed 0.61% at 10:20 PM EDT. Among ETFs tracking benchmark indexes, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) and the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) were trading higher with sentiment in the ‘bullish’ territory. According to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), the Consumer Price Index (CPI) climbed 3.5% year-on-year, below market expectations. Meanwhile, core inflation came in at 2.6%, with prices declining 0.4% from the previous month, the largest monthly drop since May 2020. Lower energy costs drove the decline in headline inflation, with the energy index falling 5.7% in June. The softer inflation figures lowered expectations for a rate hike from the Federal Reserve. Shares of Rocket Lab (RKLB) rebounded after a six-session losing streak on Tuesday as CEO Peter Beck highlighted the company as one of the few proven commercial launch providers, calling SpaceX a “friendly rival” and noting that Rocket Lab emerged from a field of more than 100 failed challengers. RKLB stock jumped nearly 3% on Tuesday, with shares also up nearly 2% overnight. In a recent BBC interview, Beck said commercial launch remains exceptionally difficult despite billions of dollars in investment. “Despite billions of dollars and over 100 companies trying, there has actually only been two companies to pop out the other end,” with a regular and reliable launch service, he said, in a discussion that also touched on Rocket Lab’s rivalry with SpaceX. “Launch and a commercial company doing launch still remains extremely rare,” Beck added. Beck called SpaceX a “friendly rival” and said space companies often compete for one contract before working together on another: “You can be competing tooth and tail for a particular contract” and later team up to deliver it, he said. Rocket Lab can also benefit when rivals win as it supplies components such as reaction wheels, star trackers and solar panels.” “We can go head to head with a traditional space prime and then lose,” Beck said. “And then the next day, there’s a purchase order.” Beck called Rocket Lab an end-to-end space company spanning satellites, launch and services from orbit: “We build satellites, we launch them on our rockets and we provide services from space,” he said. Pointing to SpaceX’s Falcon 9 and Starlink model, Beck added: “They’re able to do all those things. And we’re able to do those too.” William Blair analyst Louie DiPalma recently named Rocket Lab and Blue Origin among the strongest challengers to SpaceX, though he said SpaceX still holds more than 90% of the launch market. Rocket Lab is advancing its competitive vertical integration strategy through its $8 billion acquisition of Iridium Communications, which would add a global network, spectrum, and recurring satellite service revenue. The company recently completed a full-duration burn of its Archimedes Vacuum engine, an important step toward the first flight of its reusable Neutron rocket. Rocket Lab said it was “critical preparation for Neutron’s first flight.” Beck has told Stocktwits earlier that Rocket Lab is “pushing very hard” to launch Neutron by the fourth quarter of 2026, while cautioning that the challenge is not merely reaching orbit but proving the rocket can return and be reused. “If we just had to go up, it’s super easy, we’d be in orbit by now,” he previously said. Rocket Lab also completed the U.S. Space Force’s Victus Haze mission, launching 16 hours and 42 minutes after receiving notice and completing spacecraft commissioning and proximity operations ahead of schedule. The company supplied the launch vehicle, spacecraft and orbital operations under one contract, offering a practical demonstration of the integrated model Beck outlined in the interview. Shares of top software companies, including ServiceNow and Salesforce, fell on Tuesday after IBM reported preliminary quarterly results showing acute weakness in its software business and said clients were shifting spending to AI servers faster than anticipated. ServiceNow stock declined 5.8%, while Adobe and Salesforce’s shares dropped 4.3% and 2.1%, respectively. Software heavyweight Microsoft closed 1.6% lower as well. The group edged higher in overnight trading, led by Microsoft, which rose 0.4%. "In the last few ⁠weeks of June, we saw clients shift their quarterly capex spend toward servers, storage, and memory purchases to secure supply-constrained infrastructure ahead of ​expected price increases," CEO Arvind Krishna said in a letter to investors. "While we anticipated some supply-chain related impact in our expectations, we did not anticipate ​the magnitude of the capex reprioritization," Krishna said, adding that the company “faltered” and "numerous large deals" had failed to close as expected. IBM said the weakness was largely in its mainframe business, which sells high-end enterprise computers and related software that power mission-critical workloads, including processing massive volumes of transactions for banks, governments, airlines, and retailers. It also noted that businesses were prioritizing cybersecurity due to recent advances in AI, including the release of Anthropic’s powerful Mythos technology. IBM expects second-quarter revenue to rise 1% to $17.2 billion, with 5% growth in its software business and a 7% decline in its infrastructure business. The bottom-line figures were rather concerning, with the gross profit margin expected to drop by 100 basis points to 57.7%. IBM shares dropped a record 25.2% on Tuesday. The company will issue the full quarterly report on July 22. The comments intensified concerns about AI-driven disruption across the software industry, fears that have been building for months and weighing on software stocks. Names such as Adobe, Salesforce, and Intuit have been among the hardest-hit tech stocks this year, prompting investors to debate whether the selloff has gone too far. Could be an inflection point if positive.” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. General Fusion Group Ltd. (GFUZ) made history on Monday, becoming the first pure-play nuclear fusion energy company to trade on a major public stock exchange. In an exclusive interview with Stocktwits, CEO Greg Twinney argued that fusion is not just a cleaner alternative to fission but is a fundamentally larger market opportunity. GFUZ stock surged 21% on its debut, added over 25% on Tuesday, and was trading about 2.5% lower in the overnight session. The Vancouver-based company, backed by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, among others, went public through a SPAC merger with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp. III, which provided General Fusion with approximately $150 million in cash. Earlier, Twinney told the Wall Street Journal that the funding is sufficient to meet the scientific milestones required by its demonstration machine. The listing arrives at a pivotal moment. Surging electricity demand driven by the AI boom, the global spread of electrification, and the energy appetite of large-scale computing has renewed urgency around new sources of firm, clean power. Fusion has attracted growing investment and government attention as a potential long-term answer. According to the Financial Times, the number of private fusion companies has more than doubled over the past five years, intensifying competition at a time when the technology is still roughly a decade from commercialization. General Fusion is targeting its first commercial plant around 2035. Twinney's bull case for fusion starts with what it doesn't produce. Unlike fission, fusion does not generate long-lived radioactive waste, does not use fuels that could be weaponized, and carries no risk of a meltdown. "Fusion is just inherently safe. We're not needing to engineer safety into it in the same way that you need to with fission," he told Stocktwits. "When fusion fails, it kind of just fails safely and there's not really any fallout from that." That safety profile has a direct commercial implication: regulators around the world are moving to govern fusion "in a much lighter way" than conventional nuclear, Twinney said, which he believes creates the potential to site fusion plants closer to population centers and industrial demand. That's a significant advantage over fission, which requires remote, heavily secured facilities. "We get all the benefits that fission can provide without the downsides," he said. There's another significant advantage. Fusion reactors primarily use deuterium, which can be extracted from seawater and is "massively abundant." The other component, tritium, is rarer in nature but can be bred through the interaction of a neutron and lithium. Fission, by contrast, relies on uranium and other finite sources. "The overall market size because of the safety profile and the abundance of fuel in fusion is much bigger than fission," Twinney said. While advanced nuclear companies such as Oklo Inc. (OKLO) and NuScale Power Corp. (SMR) are often thought of as being closer to commercialization than fusion technology, Twinney said that the gap may not be as large as investors assume. While the road to commercialization for fusion technology has its challenges, including achieving reactor durability, tritium fuel breeding, economic viability, and the ability to efficiently extract and convert fusion energy into electricity, he argues small modular reactor (SMR) timelines also struggle with regulatory hurdles that can make timelines less predictable than they appear today. "I know that the timelines for SMRs, which can be very unpredictable due to regulations and those types of things, [are] probably not that different," he said. According to Twinney, the combination of abundant fuel supplies and a lighter regulatory framework could ultimately enable fusion to scale faster than conventional nuclear technologies once commercial viability has been demonstrated. However, Twinney does not view fusion and fission as mutually exclusive technologies. "They will be complementing each other," he said. "And I think that fusion kind of rounds out the nuclear circle if you think about it that way," he added. When asked about criticism from former Commonwealth Fusion Systems CTO Dan Brunner, who, in a recent interview with the Financial Times, said General Fusion's commercialization timeline was "very hard to believe," Twinney said the company’s timelines were based on real experimental results from its Lawson Machine 26. The machine is designed to demonstrate that plasma can be heated through mechanical compression rather than superconducting magnets or high-powered lasers, he said, adding that the company's early results validated the operating principles behind its MTF approach that are “not based on fiction or papers being written.” The timelines “are based on our real results from machines that we have built and operated and then eventually written papers on. But those are real results papers, not theoretical papers,” he said. Twinney also emphasized that General Fusion's approach could offer a cost advantage over many competing technologies. While many other fusion developers rely on expensive superconducting magnets, high-powered lasers, or advanced materials that have yet to be proven at commercial scale, General Fusion's Magnetized Target Fusion (MTF) system uses mechanical compression and a liquid-lithium wall that can protect reactor components from neutron damage, help with breeding tritium fuel, and absorbing fusion energy as heat that can be converted into electricity using conventional steam turbines. In an earlier interview with Stocktwits, Chief Strategy Officer Megan Wilson had also pointed to the economic advantages of MTF, which eliminate the need for expensive magnets, targets, lasers, or exotic, not-yet-invented materials. The technology also eliminates the need for frequent replacement of components damaged by neutron exposure, she had said. “Our plants are designed to be cost-competitive compared to coal, steam, and natural gas,” she had said then. “They are expected to deliver four times as much energy per unit of fuel as fission, without long-lived radioactive waste, positioning them as the superior nuclear technology for sustainable growth.” By avoiding costly magnets and lasers and using existing industrial technologies, Twinney said he believes General Fusion has a clearer path to building an economically viable power plant, as the company’s design has from the beginning aimed to avoid the major barriers to commercializing fusion. "What we are trying to do at General Fusion, and our power plant design from the beginning, has been we want to avoid the major barriers to commercializing fusion. Not just demonstrate a bunch of fusion, but actually avoid the barriers to commercializing it," he said. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around GFUZ stock is ‘bullish’ amid ‘high’ message volumes.
